original_query: SELECT t2.EMPNO, t2.ENAME, t2.JOB, t2.MGR, t2.HIREDATE, t2.SAL, t2.COMM, t2.DEPTNO, t2.SLACKER, t3.DEPTNO AS DEPTNO0, t3.NAME FROM (SELECT EMPNO, ENAME, JOB, MGR, HIREDATE, SAL, COMM, DEPTNO, SLACKER FROM EMP ORDER BY SAL FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY) AS t2 LEFT JOIN (SELECT * FROM DEPT) AS t3 ON t2.DEPTNO = t3.DEPTNO ORDER BY t2.SAL FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY
rewritten_query:
SELECT e.EMPNO, e.ENAME, e.JOB, e.MGR, e.HIREDATE, e.SAL, e.COMM, e.DEPTNO, e.SLACKER,
       d.DEPTNO AS DEPTNO0, d.NAME
FROM EMP e
LEFT JOIN DEPT d ON e.DEPTNO = d.DEPTNO
ORDER BY e.SAL
FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Flatten the unnecessary derived table `(SELECT * FROM DEPT)` into a direct LEFT JOIN on DEPT; DEPT.DEPTNO is a primary key so the join is one-to-one and does not change row count.
Remove the redundant outer FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY: the inner top-10 already limits rows to 10 and the DEPT join is one-to-one. Keep a single final ORDER BY e.SAL to guarantee result ordering.
Replace the explicit column projection in the EMP derived table with a direct reference to EMP via an alias, eliminating the redundant projection layer.

The join to DEPT already uses the dept_pkey index; the dominant cost is the full parallel sort of ~45M EMP rows for the top-N by SAL. Create an index on EMP(SAL) so the planner can read rows in SAL order and stop after 10 rows (Limit -> Nested Loop Left Join -> Index Scan), avoiding the massive sort.
No constant expressions to fold; the rewrite consists of structural simplification and index usage.
